source.title: The Swampland Conjectures: A Bridge from Quantum Gravity to Particle Physics

accepted.question_text: Can the Weak Gravity Conjecture for quantum gravity with a U(1) gauge symmetry be established by a rigorous proof, rather than only by heuristic black-hole and remnant arguments? In the formulation considered here, the conjecture constrains charged spectra and ultraviolet cutoffs so that gravity is not stronger than the gauge interaction in the relevant charged sector.

evidence.quote: a rigorous proof is still an open question

accepted.question_text: What microscopic mechanism explains the Swampland Distance Conjecture, namely the claim that an effective gravitational theory breaks down at infinite distance in field space because an infinite tower of states becomes light, and how generally is that mechanism tied to string-theoretic dualities, decompactification limits, or tensionless strings?

evidence.quote: not fully clear at the moment

accepted.question_text: What are the cobordism branes or end-of-the-world defects required by the Cobordism Conjecture for the ten-dimensional superstring theories other than the examples explicitly identified in the source, such as the Horava-Witten boundary for eleven-dimensional M-theory and O8-planes for type IIA theory?

Can full lattice computations determine whether the Standard Model QCD vacuum forms the metastable de Sitter states suggested by large-N extrapolations at fixed Yukawa couplings, a question that affects the swampland-motivated proposed upper bound on the electroweak Higgs vacuum expectation value?

Mapped a 30-page review article. Major sections include Introduction; The Swampland Conjectures; Implications for Particle Physics; and Final Comments. Relevant subsections cover absence of global symmetries and cobordisms, the Weak Gravity Conjecture, distance conjectures, compactifications of the Standard Model, Festina Lente, massless photons, and gauge groups.

The introduction lists broad particle-physics problems and explains the review scope, but most of those problems are ambient motivation rather than source-formulated open questions. No accepted candidate was taken from this section.
